'''Wijsman convergence''' is a variation of [[Hausdorff convergence]] suitable for work with [[unbounded set]]s.
Intuitively, Wijsman convergence is to convergence in the [[Hausdorff metric]] as [[pointwise convergence]] is to [[uniform convergence]].

==History==

The convergence was defined by [[Robert Wijsman]].<ref>{{cite journal
| last = Wijsman
| first = Robert A.
| title = Convergence of sequences of convex sets, cones and functions. II
| journal = Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.
| volume = 123
| year = 1966
| pages = 32&ndash;45
| doi = 10.2307/1994611
| issue = 1
| publisher = American Mathematical Society
| jstor = 1994611
| doi-access = free
}} {{MathSciNet|id=0196599}}</ref>
The same definition was used earlier by [[Zdeněk Frolík]].<ref>Z. Frolík, Concerning topological convergence of sets, Czechoskovak Math. J. 10 (1960), 168–180</ref>
Yet earlier, Hausdorff in his book ''[[Grundzüge der Mengenlehre]]'' defined so called ''closed limits'';
for [[proper metric space]]s it is the same as Wijsman convergence.

==Definition==

Let (''X'',&nbsp;''d'') be a metric space and let Cl(''X'') denote the collection of all ''d''-closed subsets of ''X''. For a point ''x''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''X'' and a set ''A''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;Cl(''X''), set

:<math>d(x, A) = \inf_{a \in A} d(x, a).</math>

A sequence (or [[Net (mathematics)|net]]) of sets ''A''<sub>''i''</sub>&nbsp;∈&nbsp;Cl(''X'') is said to be '''Wijsman convergent''' to ''A''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;Cl(''X'') if, for each ''x''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''X'',

:<math>d(x, A_{i}) \to d(x, A).</math>

Wijsman convergence induces a [[topology]] on Cl(''X''), known as the '''Wijsman topology'''.

==Properties==

* The Wijsman topology depends very strongly on the metric ''d''. Even if two metrics are uniformly equivalent, they may generate different Wijsman topologies.
* '''Beer's theorem''': if (''X'',&nbsp;''d'') is a [[complete space|complete]], [[separable space|separable]] metric space, then Cl(''X'') with the Wijsman topology is a [[Polish space]], i.e. it is separable and metrizable with a complete metric.
* Cl(''X'') with the Wijsman topology is always a [[Tychonoff space]]. Moreover, one has the '''Levi-Lechicki theorem''': (''X'',&nbsp;''d'') is separable [[if and only if]] Cl(''X'') is either metrizable, [[first-countable space|first-countable]] or [[second-countable space|second-countable]].
* If the pointwise convergence of Wijsman convergence is replaced by uniform convergence (uniformly in ''x''), then one obtains Hausdorff convergence, where the Hausdorff metric is given by

::<math>d_{\mathrm{H}} (A, B) = \sup_{x \in X} \big| d(x, A) - d(x, B) \big|.</math>

: The Hausdorff and Wijsman topologies on Cl(''X'') coincide if and only if (''X'',&nbsp;''d'') is a [[totally bounded space]].
